Help

Setup, account switching, and troubleshooting.

First setupSwitchingPassword promptsRecoveryContact

First setup

  1. Install the app, then open Claude Shannigans from Applications. It lives in the menu bar.
  2. Let important Claude agents finish before saving or switching a login. Save Current Login briefly quits and reopens Claude.
  3. Choose Discover Accounts to find local account stores. Discovery alone does not save a working login.
  4. Choose Save Current Login for the account currently signed in to Claude.
  5. Use Add Account, switch to it, and sign in through Claude itself. Open its Code tab, then choose Finish Sign-In in Shannigans.

Repeat for each account. Accounts are identified by email.

When an account runs out

  1. Finish or stop the active agents you care about.
  2. Click an account, or choose Next. Next selects the most-used eligible alternate account that still has session and weekly quota.
  3. Shannigans asks Claude to quit gracefully, backs up session metadata, activates the saved login, and reopens Claude.
  4. Open your local Code conversation and resume it. An interrupted running agent does not resume itself.

If Claude refuses to quit or takes too long, switching stops before rotating the profiles. Shannigans does not force-kill it.

100% is a usage reading, not a shutdown order. Claude may continue working for a while. Shannigans never switches automatically at a threshold.

What the numbers mean

Session used % / weekly used %. Not remaining. The weekly reset date and countdown are shown per account.

Enable Live Usage for authenticated read-only checks. Background refreshes run about once a minute. Without it, the app reads Claude's local cache and labels the result as cached. Failed, expired, or unavailable readings show as unknown; Next skips them.

Why is my Mac asking for a password?

Optional live usage checks read encrypted Claude Desktop login cookies. macOS may ask permission to access Claude Safe Storage in your login Keychain. Shannigans explains this before allowing an interactive prompt.

The password belongs to your Mac's login Keychain, usually your Mac login password. Enter it only in the macOS dialog, never into Shannigans or this website.

Always Allow remembers access for the app. Allow or Allow Once can mean more prompts when another account is checked. Not Now leaves interactive access disabled. Background refreshes never trigger password prompts.

These are full login cookies, not narrowly scoped usage tokens. They are decrypted in memory and sent only to claude.ai. Only usage numbers, reset times, and sanitized status are cached by the usage checker. You can leave Live Usage off.

What follows the switch?

Local Claude Code conversations and local workspace state are the focus. Cloud Chat and Cowork histories, cloud artifacts, sidebar groups, and scheduled-task registrations remain with their original account.

Large local session and runtime directories are shared through stable links. Account-specific session metadata is synchronized. Entire multi-gigabyte profiles are not copied on every switch. The last five session backups are retained by default; saved login profiles are not pruned as backups.

Something stopped halfway

Use Recover Interrupted Switch when the app offers it. Recovery may leave Claude stopped so you can inspect the result. The CLI equivalent is:

claude-code-account-flip repair

Don't rename, unlink, or delete profile folders by hand. They contain login state and shared session links. A missing, ambiguous, or unexpected storage layout is a reason to stop, not a reason to guess.

Updating the old development app

Quit Claude Account Switcher, the utility, before opening Claude Shannigans. You do not need to quit Claude merely to update the switcher. Remove the old utility's application bundle after the new one is installed.

The new name keeps the existing bundle identity and data location: ~/Library/Application Support/Claude Account Switcher. No profile migration is required. Don't run two copies.

After public release, Homebrew updates use brew upgrade --cask synestheticsystems/tap/claude-shannigans. If an older account-flip script conflicts with the CLI link, inspect its location before replacing it; do not use a blanket force-install.

Removing the app

Quit Shannigans and remove its app bundle, or uninstall its Homebrew cask. Uninstalling deliberately leaves saved logins, backups, and session data alone.

Because active Claude storage may link into shared data, deleting Shannigans' support folder can break Claude or erase sessions. There is currently no automatic profile-data cleanup. Ask for help before removing that data.

Support

Open a support issue with your macOS, Claude, and Shannigans versions, what you clicked, and what happened. Issues are public: don't attach cookies, profile folders, account emails, or unredacted session logs.
